HEALTH OF SIR GILBERT GREENALL.

Yesterday, the rumour was current that the mem- ber for Warrington, Sir Gilbert Greenell, had died at his residence, Walton Hall, The rumour happily proved to be unfounded, as from inquiries made, it was ascertained that, though Sir Cillbert's health has been in a critical condition for sometime past be has, during the present week, been in rather, better condition than usual.
COLLIERS AND THEIR WAGES.

ANOTHER ADVANCE DEMANDED. On Sunday afternoon a mass meeting of the colliera of St. Helens and district was held, in Mr. Fletcher's coach-house, Bickerstaff-st., St. Helens, to consider the decisions of the recent National Conference of miners' delegates at Birmingham. Notwithstanding the inclement weather there was a large attendance. Mr. T. Glover, the miner's agent, formally addressed the men, and said that there were several questions of an important char- acter discussed at the Conference, at which there were representatives of 101, 338 miners present, and be thought such a body could speak with great influence and power. In regard to the proposed Eight Hours Bill the conference decided to do all I they possibly could to secure its passing by Parlia- ment and the/ hoped when it became law it woul& be beneficial to the miners of the Kingdom. (Ap- plause). In regard to the Employers' Liability Act the conference considered it an injustice that min- ers' should be compelled to sign themselves out of the provisions of the Act in regard to compensation by the employers in case of accident. They were told that they wanted their employers' money but what the miners' wanted was that their mine's should be made and kept safe, that the masters should provide everything that was necessary for the safety of the limbs and lives of those men he employed (applause). 'I hey also wished legislation [to. prevent unskilled workmen being allowed to work in mines, and with that end were seeking to make it impossible for anyone to obtain dangerous work down a mine who had not served an appren- ticeship commenced before he was 16 years of age. There had been a frequent loss of life through unskilled workmen, and they now sought to prevent it. They also wanted more sub-Inspectors of mines to make proper and complete examinations at more regular intervals than was possible at the present time. In regard to the wages the Confer- ence thought it was time they asked for another ten per cent. advance. (Applause.) He maintained that during the past. two years the average prices of coal had been increased 821 per cent., and he 'thought the colliers were entitled to a greater pro- portion of that increase than they had received. The colliers were only Asking for that to which they had a perfect right, and they meant to enforce their demand. They would come out on strike, if their demand was not conceded, and upon the masters would rest the blame. The following resolution was then unanimously passed : "That this meet- ing of miners heartily agree with the work of the National Conference at Birmingham on the Eight Hours Bill, the Employers Liability Act, unskilled labour in mines, sub-inspector of mines, and espe- cially on the wage question in determining to de- mand another 10 per cent advance, and we pledge ourselves to do all in our power to carry the same into effect."

div.head: ST. BA RNABAS' SCHOOL DISPUTE.
div.p: ST. BA RNABAS' SCHOOL DISPUTE.

During the week nothing fresh has occurred in connection with the unfortunate dispute at St. Bamabas' Schools, Warrington, but the hearing of the action for detenue, entered in the County Court, has been fixed for Thursday next. The managers claim from Mr. Woollamt and Miss Parsons, damages for alleged illegal removal and detention of registers and other articles belonging to the schools. Mr. Tomlinson, solictor, Preston, has .the case in hand on behalf of the managers, and Mr. W. H. J. Jenkins, solicitor, Warrington, has been retained on behalf of the Teachers' Association. It is stated that Mr. Lynn, the Counsel for the National Association of School Teachers will appear to con- duct the defence on their behalf.

div.p: DEATH THIS MOkNING
MR. McMINNIES.

It is with deep regret that We have to inform our readers of the death, at half-past one this (Saturday) morning, of Mr. J. G. McMinnies, J.P., ex-Member for the borough, and president of the Liberal Association. It will 134 remembered that Mr. Mc- Minnies refrained, in 1885, from offering himielf for re-election as &ember for Warrington on acci,iunt of

his health. Since then he had been more or less ailing, as our readers will be aware from the instances in which he had had to apologise for being unable to attend, and preside over vari- ous Liberal meetings. He had, however, at- tended all the meetings he could, often when he was ouffering, and at mdch personal in- convenience. His health unfortunately gradually became worse with advancing years, but it was not until about a fortnight ago that it was thought his condition had become really critical. He

was able to rise and remain in bis library, where. he spent most of his time' - until early in this week, when one night he suddenly became seriously ill, and had to be assisted to his bedroom. There he remained during the past few days,. receiving at the hands of his medical attendant, Dr. Starkey Smith, all the aid that it was possibl e to give. He had been more or less unconscious during this latest attack, and it was felt that the end was near. His nephew, Mr. William McMinnies. had been with him since Thursday morning. Mr. Mc- Minnies, it should be mentioned, completed' his 72nd year in May last. It is hardly necessary to say that the most anxious inquiries Vero made by his friends throughout yesterday, and that. they received such information as could be given with the most gloomy forebodings. The Rev. Tonge was amongst those who called and saw 'him at an early hour yesterday morning, but he was then in' an unconscious condition.

The Warrington police were yesterday informed of the death of a child, named Ellen Shaw, five years of age, daughter of Leonard Shaw, fitter„33,l, Win- wick-road, which occurred at the infirmary on Thursday night, from burns received earlier irr the day. During the temporary absence of h..r mother, the girl seems to have attempted to reach a teapot from the hob, and in so doidg her dress brushed against the bars of the fire-place and caught tire. The child ran screaming into the yard, and out' on to the waste ground at the back of the house. lEer cries brought several neighborrs to her assistance, and she was promptly conveyed to the Infirmary, but her injuries were of so serious a nature that she died about midnight.

That' the salary of the Town Clerk shall be £5OO rer annum which shall be inclusive of everything except expenses out of pocket for telegrams, stamps, carriage of parcels, Sze., and when out of town on, Corporatioa business he shall be allowed Ist class railway fares' and cab fares, and if unavoidably detained all night the sum a£l is. Od. per day and when not ,so detained the Kula of 10s. 6th per day. M.) That ho shall not become surety for any person or rersons in respect of or for the payment of any sum or sums of money. (15.) That he shall Dot be allowed to have at any time more than one articled clerk without the sanction of the Council. And the SuleCommitteefurther recommend :—(1.) That the present Deputy Town Merle, Mr. J. Lyon Whittle, be ap- pointed the Town Clerk of the Borough of Warrington, under and subject to the foregoing terms and conditions, and that his duties commence °lathe 25th March next. (2.) That Mr. Stanley Wilson (who has been in the Town Clerk's office since 1880) be appointed Clerk in the Town Clerk's office at the salary of £lOO pert annum.. (Signed)—R. W. Francomb, John Burgess, Charles J. Holmes, Joseph Harrison, Thomas H. Sutton,. Frederick Monks. Town Hall, 25th January, 1890. . MR. lIENRY GLADSTONE'S MARRIAGE.

The marriage of Mr. Henry Gladstone and Missi Maud Rendel was celebrated, on Thursday afternoon, at St. Margaret's Church, Westminster. The Rev. Stephen Gladstone, brother of the bridegroom, conducted , the servlce, assisted by Archdeacon Farrar and the Rev. Elward Talbot. A very large number of relatives and friends of the two families were present.

-..- PRESCOT WATCHMAKERS' ASSOCIATIOX,—The annual meeting of this society was held on Monday evening, at the Crown Hotel, Mr. J. Hall presiding. The auditors report showed the society to be doing fairly well, having saved over £lOO during the yerr. The following officers were then elected for the ensuing year : President, Mr. Edwin Rimmer ; vice-president, Mr. John, Atherton; trea., Mr, John Accra: sec., Mr. Jos. Meredith; and committee Messrs. John Beasley, Henry Simm, John Starkey, Thomas Atherton, Wm. Meredith, James Hold- ing,John Case, Wm. Ctitchley, K McCarty, Jonathan [ Finney. Jos. ease, Thos. Rose and Joint Cross.
ECCLESIASTICAL.
The Rey. G. If: Williams, formerly curate of Holy Trinity Church, Warrington. has been licensed to the stipendiary curacy of Christ Church, Southport.

LICENSING CHANGES. Yesterday, at the Warrington Police Court, an off-license for premisee in Winwick-rd. was trans- ferred from Thos. Ctitchley to Thos. Perrin, and the license of the Higher Angel, Buttermarket-st., transferred from James Higginson to Thomas Critchiey.•

div.head: SANKEINST. CIRCUS.
div.p: THE SANKEINST. CIRCUS.

During the week there have been good houses at the Sankey-st. Circus,. which has been opened by Mr. Francis, who has brought to Warrington a powerful company oi sedates, and a stud of trained horses and ponies. The progralnme submitted nightly has been of an interesting , and amusing ,character, and has given much satisfaction to the. "patrons ot the circus. There are clever riding feats, conjuring tricks, merry clowns, and performances of trained animals that are well worth witnessing. An attractive programme is advertised for next week.

div.head: WARRTNOTON SCHOOL OF ART.
div.p: WARRTNOTON SCHOOL OF ART.

Another of the series of illustrations of the art, architecture, and scenery of various countries, was givsui on Wednesday evening, in the School of Art, Museuni-'street, there being a nnmerous attendance of visitors and students. An imaginary visit was paid toJapan, and the audience were shown, by the aid of the limelight lentern, the beauties of the scenery, and the peculiarities, habits, and customs of the Jitpanese race' a very pleasant and profitable hour being spent. Mr. T. Fletcher again manipu- lated the lantern, and the reflections on the screen were explained by Mr. It. Garnett, sun., of Penketh.

OXIMEDGE MaiSION COTWEICT. A very successful concert of the aeries was held was held at the Mission, orrSaturday evening, under the presidency of Mr. .1: Willett. The friends at Bank Quay Mission furnished the. following pro- gramme, which was admirably rendered :—Glee, glee party ; song, Miss- Brough ;due, Misses Mills and Dunn; song, Miss- Ashley;, reading. Mills; duet, Misses Brough and doyley ; song, Miss Ashley; recitations, Mr. Boons; song, Mr. Dunn; glee, glee party.. A hearty vote of thanks was tendered by the nreeting to. the per- formers for their efforts in making the evening's entertainment Ss very enjoyable.. WYCLIFFE TEMPERANCE Soc. The first of a series of public temperance meet- ing in connection with Viycliffe Tbmperance Society was held, in Wycliffe Hall,, on Wednesday evening. The Ray. J. Yonge presided,, and there was a fair attendance. The Chairman,, in opening the proceedings, referred to 'thew Band ef Hope in connection with Wycliffe and said that those who had the management of it lead reason to be encouraged. At the first meeting three weeks ago there were only 47; present, at the next meeting that number was doubled, and the attendances had gone on increasing since. Mr. Yiinge referred to the evidence they. were contaitally being: provided with in the newspapers of the evils broaght about by intemperance, and he expressed a hope that Christian people would take a. deeper interest in that question, as mall other social questions, which roust have a far larger place in the minds aud hearts of Christian people in the fauna 011'mm the past. An address was also.given .by Mr. COndon, of the United Kingdom Alliance. A recitation. "The Sign- board," was given byJennie Bailey, and a dtalogue "The Irish Schoolmaster," Was taken part in by Mr. C. H. Mills (scboolmaster),4,lD.,Owen, S. Reyes, r 11. Shaw, T. Ball, Wl3all, E. Chernock. P. Roberts, , and W. Woodcock.. B. Evans recited "The Moderate 'Drinker's soliloquy,' and a song was given by Harry Shaw. •

WIDNES LOCAL BOARD. IN PARLIAMENT,—SESSION 1890. MANCHESTER SHIP CANAL (TIDAL OPENINGS, Acc) AND WIDNES BRINE SUPPLY. Pursuant to the Act 35 and 36 Vic., cap. 91, and in com- pliance with a requisition duly made to me, I, as the Chairman of the Local Board for the District, of Whines, in the County of Lancaster, DO HEREBY SUMMON A MEETING of the Owners and Ratepayers of the said District to be held in the Town Hall, Widnes, in the said district, on Tuesday, the 4th day of February, 1890, at half-past Eleven o'clock in the forenoon, for the purpose, if thought desirable, of approving and giving consent to the opposing by the said Local Board of the undermentioned Bills, or either of them, now pending in Parliament, namely : I "A Bill to alter certain Works authorized by the Man- chester Ship Canal Act, 1885 ; and for other purposes," also "A Bill for incorporating and conferring Powers upon the Whines Brine Supply Company ; and for other purposes," and also to sanction the application of the General District Rate, or other the Public Funds or Rates under the control of the said Local Board, to the payment of the costs and expenses attending such opposition. Given under my hand this 20th day of January, 1890. FRED. H. GOSSAGE, Chairman and Summoning Officer.
